text.p: FAI Insurances Ltd said on Tuesday it expected a stronger profit result in the year to June 30, 1997 than in the 1995/96 year just gone.
It also said it expected turnover in 1996/97 of about A$1.5 billion, up from A$1.19 billion in 1994/95.
"It is anticipated that turnover for the fiscal year ending June 1997 will be approximately A$1.5 billion and all business sectors will remain cash flow positive," FAI said.
"We expect our results to improve during the year and our budget projections indicate a stronger result than those results just released," it said.

FAI earlier reported a A$10.04 million net profit in the year to June 30, 1996, up from a A$89.84 million loss in 1994/95. It also set a one cent per share final dividend versus nil last year, taking the total to one cent, the same as in 1994/95.
Premium income net of reinsurance for the year was A$607.5 million, unchanged from the previous year. Overall losses from underwriting business fell 37 percent to A$49.7 million.
"The improvement in New South Wales CTP (Compulsory Third Party) rates and government changes to benefits were a major contributor to this improvement," FAI said.
"As well, the 39 percent increase in the Queensland CTP rates, which became effective on July 1, 1996, will have a significant impact on the portfolio in future years," it said.
"The full benefit will not be felt, however, until the year ending June 30, 1998."
FAI said an ongoing re-weighting of the investment portfolio saw performance in the sector improve despite a flat investment market.
"Oceanic Coal Australia Ltd had a very successful year reflecting the generally favourable mining conditions, coal prices and industrial relations climate prevailing throughout the year," FAI said.
FAI's shares were down one cent down at 71 cents at 2.45 p.m. (0445 GMT).
